taskNotes.01: Contract types unchanged; added CLIENT_OBLIGATIONS as the normative name of the closed code->obligation map (graph-core/src/eap/refusals.ts). Legacy claim status migration remains explicitly undecided.
taskNotes.02: Lifecycle aggregate unchanged; the MCP adapter now validates identifiers and sequence bounds before reaching it.
taskNotes.04: Horizon persistence unchanged apart from a parent_id nullability fix; new EAP tables added to the same durable path (db.ts).
taskNotes.05: incrementalGate now returns { ok, refusals } with typed EAP refusal codes and client obligations alongside the legacy reasons/warnings.
taskNotes.06: PromotionService is now repository-backed; eapPromote persists a proposed parent candidate row and aborts on a failed transition.
taskNotes.07: admitPersistentDelta is one atomic durable unit and evaluates candidates against a per-batch roundtrip index.
taskNotes.08: ContestationService is now repository-backed with durable atomic sequence allocation.
taskNotes.09: RecallWorker writes through SqliteRecallRepository; checkpoints and scars survive restart.
taskNotes.10: CapabilityGateway validates stored approvals, enforces an execution timeout with AbortSignal cancellation, records a retention-bounded durable audit log, and applies an authorization projection filter.
taskNotes.11: cognitive.* adapters run in serialized transactions with atomic sequence allocation and boundary validation.
taskNotes.12: ExternalAgentClientAdapter forwards the session token and the caller's real evidence under the host's 'evidence' field; it never fabricates evidence and never self-admits.
taskNotes.13: eap-conformance.test.ts replaced: it was a table of hardcoded verified:true literals and is now a black-box profile driven over the real MCP transport, with ADR-deferred questions listed as explicit exclusions.

testsAdded.note: contestation/capability-governance/eap-conformance counts are NEW tests added to files that already existed; promotion.test.ts gained no new test cases, only stronger assertions plus a durable repository fixture.

1_durability_state_divergence.summary: PromotionService, ContestationService, RecallWorker, CapabilityGateway and the approval store no longer own any in-memory aggregate state. All five take a SQLite-backed repository writing through the project's existing durable path (write() = SQLite + per-tenant append-only JSONL). The domain services and the MCP tool adapters now read and write the SAME rows, so they cannot diverge.

2_unbounded_memory_growth.summary: CapabilityGateway.executedOutcomes and .auditLog are deleted; idempotency and audit live in capability_executions with an explicit retention bound (DEFAULT_AUDIT_MAX_ENTRIES = 10000, configurable) enforced in the same transaction as each append. ApprovalRepository's Map is replaced by the operator_approvals table. RecallWorker's event array is a bounded ring (DEFAULT_MAX_RETAINED_EVENTS = 500) with durable progress in SQLite. The only remaining in-process Map is CapabilityGateway.classificationMap, which is static host configuration bounded by the number of registered capabilities, not accumulating state.

3_concurrency_and_sequence_races.summary: Every 'SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq),0)+1' is gone. db.ts adds allocateSequence() (a single UPSERT ... RETURNING against eap_sequences) and serialTransaction() (BEGIN IMMEDIATE, so the read-decide-write section is serialized between writers instead of racing on a DEFERRED snapshot). eapPropose, eapPromote, eapContest and eapRecall all run inside serialTransaction; allocation and the write consuming it commit as one unit. eapPromote no longer forces a sequence increment: a failed saveTransition returns STALE_BASE and aborts, and eapRecall is idempotent per contestation so a replay returns the existing case rather than burning a fresh sequence.

3_concurrency_and_sequence_races.honestCaveat: The serialization is proven structurally (BEGIN IMMEDIATE + atomic UPSERT ... RETURNING) and behaviourally via the sequence-reuse and fault-injection tests. It is NOT proven by a true multi-process concurrent load test: the host is single-threaded Bun and this repository has no multi-process harness for the cognitive tools. A cross-process stress test remains the strongest evidence that was not produced here.

4_authorization_and_validation_gaps.summary: CapabilityGateway no longer trusts the client-supplied approval object: a request may only NAME an approval id, and scope, expiry, basedOnSeq and the consumed flag are read from the operator's stored grant. An id no operator registered is APPROVAL_MISSING and the provider is never invoked. getAuditLog now requires an authenticated principal (throws without one) and returns a tagged projection — full entries only for a principal holding 'audit:read', redacted (no contractRef, no provider outcome) otherwise. eapRecall checks presence, status === 'admitted' and severity === 'invalidating' as three separate explicit conditions. eapPromote verifies the parent horizon exists as a governed horizon of the same tenant and writes the parent proposal row plus proposed candidate rows durably. ExternalAgentClientAdapter forwards the session token (refusing locally if absent) and the caller's real evidence under the host's 'evidence' field, and never substitutes a fabricated ['evidence-default'].

5_transactional_recovery_of_admitPersist.summary: Admission is now ONE durableTransaction covering gate evaluation, changeset open, cs_deltas staging and changesetCommit (durableTransaction is re-entrant, so the nested commit joins the same unit). A refusal or failure unwinds via a typed sentinel, so no orphaned cs_deltas rows and no held cell locks survive. The compensating changesetAbort calls — themselves a third transaction that could fail — are gone. Also fixed a latent ReferenceError: the refusal branch pushed onto an undeclared 'reasons' variable and would have thrown on any refused candidate.

6_per_candidate_claim_snapshot_reparse.summary: incrementalGate accepted only ClaimSnapshot[] and re-projected the entire tenant claim set to RoundtripClaim[] on every call, so an N-candidate batch did N full-tenant projections. gates.ts now exports buildRoundtripIndex(); IncrementalCtx accepts a prebuilt existingRoundtrip, and admitPersistentDelta builds it ONCE per batch alongside the single readClaims() snapshot load.
tests: packages/mcp-server/test/f001-retry5-concurrency-authz.test.ts :: 'candidate evaluation does not rebuild the tenant claim snapshot per candidate' (instruments db.query and bounds the claim-snapshot reads for a 25-candidate batch)
6_per_candidate_claim_snapshot_reparse.honestCaveat: The test bounds the number of claim SELECTs, and the projection is provably built once. It does NOT benchmark a 100k-claim tenant; the asymptotic claim (O(claims) instead of O(N x claims)) rests on reading the code, not on a measured load run.

7_capability_execution_timeout_and_cance.summary: CapabilityGateway.execute takes an explicit timeoutMs (DEFAULT_CAPABILITY_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000), creates an AbortController, passes its signal to providerAction, aborts the controller BEFORE rejecting on timeout, and clears the timer in a finally block. A timed-out execution is never recorded as a CapabilityExecuted outcome.
implementation: packages/graph-core/src/eap/capabilities.ts (providerAction signature widened to accept the signal)
tests: packages/mcp-server/test/f001-retry5-concurrency-authz.test.ts :: 'CapabilityGateway times out a hanging provider and cancels it via AbortSignal' (asserts the observed signal is aborted and that the audit table stays empty)
7_capability_execution_timeout_and_cance.honestCaveat: Cancellation is cooperative. The gateway signals abort and stops awaiting, but a provider that ignores its AbortSignal cannot be forcibly killed from here. No circuit breaker was added — repeated provider failure still costs one timeout per call.
